newsitem.title: UK: Nickel prices hit two-year low as speculators sell.
newsitem.headline: Nickel prices hit two-year low as speculators sell.

text.p: World prices of nickel slumped to their lowest level for more than two years on Monday as funds and speculators sold into the market once it dipped below the psychological $7,000-a-tonne level.
At the midday close on the London Metal Exchange (LME) benchmark three month nickel prices finished at $6,700 having hit a low of $6,650 at one point.
NICKEL PRICES hit two-year low as speculators sell

The market has suffered from an overhang of Russian metal in Europe during the last few months, and when that metal began to be delivered into more visible LME inventories, values came under pressure.
LME nickel stocks rose above 44,000 tonnes last week compared with a low of around 32,000 tonnes in July.
Surplus stocks of stainless steel has also weighed on the market throughout 1996.
Stainless steel production accounts for around two thirds of all nickel
